messages:
maria: quick FYI — CascadeFin LoRA handoff. Uploaded quick-eval pack (3 subsets: general, regulatory, code). Int4 quant run shows a regression cluster on regulatory prompts, not huge but consistent. attaching logs and eval summary.
kevin: grabbing the pack now. saw a couple of weird tokenization hits in the sample outputs (lots of <unk> around currency symbols). can you paste the tokenizer version used for the base model?
maria: base tokenizer = sentencepiece v0.1.96, vocab_sha = 7a2f9b. LOra file attached: hydra-lora-v2.merge.pt. quant config used by the engineering run: `bits=4, scheme=dynamic, group_size=128`.
ash: fwiw stitch vs merge discussion from last week — stitch keeps adapter params separate which should avoid some tokenizer remap surprises. merging into base could expose quantization noise.
kevin: confirmed. also eval-bot flagged these examples with low log-prob and high token-penalty. small snippet of failing case:
```
Prompt: "Which account is liable for client X's default under IFRS?"
Expected: mentions clause numbers, cites policy.
Model: hallucinates non-existent regulation numbers + truncates mid-sentence.
```
riley: infra check — no GPU OOMs, canary capacity stable. the int4 runtime paths completed without kernel fallback. so this looks like a model/quant interaction, not infra.
samir: eval-bot summary -> regression stats: general delta +0.2% acc, regulatory delta -3.2% acc, hallucination-rate +6.8% on regulatory subset. n=240 examples. full CSV uploaded to `/artifacts/cascadefin/3105001234/eval_summary.csv`.
maria: thanks. plan proposal: 1) try stitch (adapter-only) infer with int4 to see if behavior persists; 2) if continues, run a targeted remap of problematic tokens (currency, section symbols) and re-eval; 3) run a small warm-start full-merge + re-quant as last resort. anyone object?
kevin: +1 to that order. also propose toggling `per_channel_quant=True` for the heads and trying `clip_qparams=True` (small experiments) — sometimes reduces high-tail hallucinations.
ash: agree. add a focused eval slice for 'citation_precision' (exact mention matches) so we can track hallucination types.
samir: kicked off two jobs: stitch+int4 quickpack (job 9876) and stitch+int8 baseline (job 9877) to compare. ETA ~40m.
maria: great. when stitch results land, let's run a diff on token-level probs and the citation_precision metric. if stitch fixes it, we'll recommend CascadeFin keep adapter-only deploy in Dedicated while we iterate on merge strategy.
kevin: quick note: tokenizer remap idea — sample mapping:
```
{"$": "$", "§": "\u00A7", "€": "€"}
```
we'll generate a small remap table and pass `tokenizer.remap_table` during merge.
maria: cool. I'll hold off full-merge until we see stitch+int4. pinging @riley if we need rollback hooks added to canary policy.
riley: copied. canary rollback hook present. if model-level error rate >5% on regulatory slice we'll auto-rollback.
maria: perfect. I'll post results here once jobs finish. :thumbsup:
eval-bot: stitch+int4 job 9876 completed — preliminary: regulatory delta now -0.6% (much improved), hallucination +1.2%. details in artifact.
maria: that's promising. proceeding to run remap+stitch with `per_channel_quant=True` next. ETA 30m. thanks all :party_parrot:
